The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 07b43c6077268638), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. statement: The following statements hold over S, naturally under base change, with arbitrary retained compact profinite parameters. (i) There is a constant Ap > 1, depending only on p and the chosen Kummer generator, such that for rout/r ≥ Ap the map RΓ(DS(c, rout), O♭ ) −→ RΓ(DS(c, r), O♭ ) factors through evaluation R[0] followed by the constant inclusion. In particular, H0 (DS(c, r), O♭ ) = R, and colim r→0 RΓ(DS(c, r), O♭ ) ≃ R[0]. (ii) Ordinary and compactly supported cohomology of the line are RΓ(AS, O♭ ) ≃ R[0], RΓc(AS, O♭ ) ≃ R[−2]. (5.8) For two concentric support discs with a sufficiently large radius ratio, the map from the smaller support complex to the larger one has pure degree-two image, carried isomorphically into the final compact-support cohomology. More precisely, if Ar is the support complex for the disc of radius r and qr : Ar → R[−2] is extension of support to the whole line, the cone of qr maps cohomologically to zero after that fixed enlargement. The required ratio is uniform, also under bounded translations of the centers. (iii) For d ordered affine coordinates, the ordinary and section-germ complexes are R[0], and the compact-support complex computed by cofinal boxes is R[−2d]. Maps between box-support bounds have pure degree-2d image after a fixed enlargement in each coordinate. (iv) The analogous relative assertions with Fp coefficients hold with the base complex RΓ(S, Fp) in place of R. For S = Spa(C♭, OC♭ ) × D this base complex is C(D, Fp)[0]. With the chosen geometric orientations, extension of constants identifies these line, section-germ, and support computations with the corresponding RD computations above. The degree-two support class is unchanged by a translation of its section. Under inclusion of finitely many disjoint support discs into one larger disc, their degree-two classes add.
